chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muskān, from Muḥammad al-Ḥalabī, who said:
I asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about a man speaking during his adhan or during his iqamah, and he said: There is no harm in it.

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, the Imam being asked for the ruling
key_terms.أَذَانِهِ: his adhan, the call announcing the prayer time
key_terms.إِقَامَتِهِ: his iqamah, the call immediately preceding the start of salat
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm, indicating permissibility
key_terms.يَتَكَلَّمُ: speaks, meaning uttering speech during the adhan or iqamah

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to speak during the adhan or iqamah according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith states that speaking during the adhan or iqamah is not considered problematic. It conveys a legal ruling related to the etiquettes and permissibility of speech in the context of preparing for salat.
